ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
module_role: Standardized debug-access architecture instantiated inside virtually every Arm Cortex-based SoC. Each compliant SoC contains a Debug Access Port (DAP) consisting of: (1) a 2-pin (SWD-DP) or 4-pin (JTAG-DP) or mode-switchable (SWJ-DP) Debug Port at the wire layer, (2) a DP register file (IDCODE/DPIDR + ABORT + CTRL/STAT + SELECT + RDBUFF + TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT), and (3) one or more Access Ports (MEM-AP variants, JTAG-AP, etc.) selected by SELECT.APSEL. The MEM-AP variant bridges the DAP to the SoC's internal AHB/AXI/APB debug bus, giving the host master-class access to any memory-mapped resource including CPU debug-control registers, peripherals, and memories.

integration_overview.wire_directions: SWCLK: host → target (host-driven). SWDIO: bidirectional with explicit 1-bit Turnaround direction-change periods. nTRST (optional, SWJ-DP only): host → target. SWO (optional, trace): target → host.
integration_overview.no_chip_select: There is no separate chip-select line. In multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) the per-target selection is done via the TARGETSEL transaction after a JTAG-to-SWD selection sequence.
integration_overview.addressing_at_protocol_layer: DP registers addressed by A[2:3] bits in the 8-bit Request packet. AP registers addressed by SELECT.APSEL (which AP) + SELECT.APBANKSEL (which bank within the AP) + Request.A[2:3] (which register in the bank).
integration_overview.test_logic_independent_of_functional_log: SWD pins are dedicated debug pins (SWCLK + SWDIO are not shared with functional logic in most parts). The SWJ-DP variant shares the JTAG TMS/TCK pad-pair with SWD's SWDIO/SWCLK, but the JTAG-side functional path is gated off in SWD mode.
integration_overview.handshake: Synchronous shift; target signals OK/WAIT/FAULT per transaction. Implicit posted-read pipeline. 50-cycle line reset is the universal out-of-band recovery.

interface_categories: Debug Host (USB-to-SWD probe) — drives SWCLK and bidirectionally drives or tri-states SWDIO; sequences 46-bit transactions; manages SELECT for AP banking; reads RDBUFF for posted-read recovery; performs line reset for recovery.
SWJ-DP Wire-Level Controller (target side) — implements SWD shift register + 46-bit transaction state machine + line-reset detector + SWJ selection-sequence detector.
SW-DP / JTAG-DP Debug Port Layer — exposes DP register set (IDCODE/DPIDR + ABORT + CTRL/STAT + SELECT + RDBUFF + ADIv5.1+ TARGETID/DLPIDR/EVENTSTAT).
AP Bus — internal bus between DP and AP instances; up to 256 APs.
MEM-AP Instance — bridges DAP transactions to a system bus (AHB / AXI / APB / etc.); CSW + TAR + DRW + BD0-BD3 + CFG + BASE + IDR.
JTAG-AP Instance — bridges DAP transactions to a downstream legacy JTAG TAP daisy chain.
CoreSight ROM Table — published at MEM-AP BASE; enumerates the SoC's debug components.
Debug Components — CPUs, FPB, DWT, ITM, ETM, CTI, TPIU, ROM-of-ROMs, reachable via the system bus from MEM-AP.
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single target SWD — one host, one SoC, 2-pin connection.
Multi-drop SWD (ADIv5.2) — one host, two or more SoCs sharing SWDIO/SWCLK; per-target selection via TARGETSEL.
SWJ-DP mode-switched — single SoC supports both SWD and JTAG via the same pads; mode is selected at runtime.
SWD + SWO trace — SWD pair plus a dedicated SWO trace output pin for ITM/DWT trace capture.

daisy_chain_rules.no_serial_daisy_chain: Unlike JTAG, SWD does NOT support a serial daisy chain. Multiple targets share SWDIO/SWCLK in parallel (multi-drop ADIv5.2 only); selection is by TARGETSEL, not by physical chain order.
daisy_chain_rules.multidrop_selection_rule: After a line reset + JTAG-to-SWD sequence + DP TARGETSEL write matching TARGETID.TPARTNO + DLPIDR.TINSTANCE, the addressed target drives ACK on subsequent transactions; all other targets ignore the bus.

default_signal_values_when_omitted.SWCLK_pull: Recommended pull-down (so the bus is quiescent if no host is connected). Some probes drive SWCLK actively at idle level.
default_signal_values_when_omitted.SWDIO_pull: Recommended pull-up (idle HIGH = line-reset compatible). When no host is connected, SWDIO drifts HIGH and the SW-DP stays in reset state.
default_signal_values_when_omitted.nTRST_pull: Recommended pull-up (de-asserted) for SWJ-DP variants exposing nTRST.

soc_dependent_items: Number of APs implemented (1 MEM-AP for single-core MCU; multiple MEM-APs + APB-AP + JTAG-AP for multi-core SoC).
MEM-AP variant (AHB-AP / APB-AP / AXI-AP — depends on the on-chip debug bus).
Presence of nTRST pad (mostly historical; SWD-only parts omit it).
Presence of SWO trace pin (some Cortex-M0 parts omit it).
CoreSight ROM Table contents (depends on what debug components the SoC includes: FPB / DWT / ITM / ETM / CTI / TPIU / ROM-of-ROMs).
DPIDR DESIGNER + PARTNO + VERSION fields (silicon mask-level fixed).
TARGETID + DLPIDR values (silicon mask-level fixed; ADIv5.1+).
Board-level pull-up on SWDIO and pull-down on SWCLK.
Debug-probe connector format (Arm 10-pin Cortex Debug header, 20-pin Cortex Debug+ETM, TC2050 needle-probe, etc.).

low_power_modes.CSYSPWRUPREQ_CDBGPWRUPREQ: The CTRL/STAT register provides CDBGPWRUPREQ + CSYSPWRUPREQ bits — the host sets them at session start to bring up debug + system power domains. CDBGPWRUPACK + CSYSPWRUPACK confirm the request.
low_power_modes.SWCLK_stopped: When the host stops SWCLK between transactions, the SW-DP wire-level FSM holds its idle state. Dynamic current drops to leakage.
low_power_modes.TAP_runs_in_chip_sleep: Since SWD pins are dedicated and the SW-DP can be in its own always-on debug-power domain, the SWD interface can remain alive even when the SoC's functional clocks are gated off — this is how 'wake on debug' and 'debug during deep sleep' work on Cortex-M MCUs.

compatibility_notes: ADIv5.1 (2009) adds TARGETID + DLPIDR + EVENTSTAT registers in DP higher banks.
ADIv5.2 (2017+) adds multi-drop SWD, long-address TAR (64-bit), and large-data DRW (≥ 64-bit).
ADIv6 (Arm IHI 0074, 2019+) is the successor architecture; SWD is preserved but adds hierarchical ROM Tables and extended APs (AXI4-AP, APBv4-AP).
SWD and JTAG-DP share the same DP register model — host software can target either with the same DP/AP-level API.
CoreSight ROM Tables follow the format defined by the CoreSight Architecture Specification (Arm IHI 0029).
